data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only when the test's installation ritual makes the subject's failure visible before the test can pass, and describes its subject when the subject's own guard structure already determines the pass/fail distribution.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the shown-to-fail-first order is not actually enforced by compile.py but is only a report ordering convention, the asymmetry collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 mutation was a content-edit hole not reachable by the test harness's mutation operators, the loss is an artifact of mutation selection, not a property of the test.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the ordinarily-guarded modules had guards written after the tests, the description/constraint attribution is reversed.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In the shown-to-fail-first installation, the mutation is planted so that the test must fail first. This forces the test to constrain the mutated subject because the failure is a prerequisite for the test being counted. In the ordinarily-guarded modules, the existing guards (e.g. registry.py's 6/6) already encode the failure modes, so the test merely describes what the guard has already constrained.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
